comments.body: Thanks Ben, Ill take a look.

Found the root cause. This op is a pooling op that has been generalized to a `linalg.generic`. This is going to cause all sort of badness (we wont vectorize this correctly cause we dont know that is a pooling op, etc.). So looks like something changed in MHLO for this. @jpienaar or @rsuderman any ideas? (cant see anything obvious from the commit list)

```
#map2 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2, d3, d4) -> (d0 * 2 + d3, d1 * 2 + d4, d2)>
#map3 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2, d3, d4) -> (d3, d4)>
#map4 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2, d3, d4) -> (d0, d1, d2)>
        %2 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [#map2, #map3, #map4], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel", "parallel", "reduction", "reduction"]} ins(%0, %1 : tensor<114x114x64xf32>, tensor<3x3xf32>) outs(%cst : tensor<56x56x64xf32>) {
        ^bb0(%in: f32, %in_0: f32, %out: f32):
          %3 = arith.maxf %out, %in : f32
          linalg.yield %3 : f32
        } -> tensor<56x56x64xf32>
```

Ill try to have a WAR for this that doesnt fail compilation (so good to have anyway), but that only helps compilation. This would cause regressions.

issue.body:
This integrate caused a regression in bufferization that leads to large stack allocations when none should be required:
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/commit/cc0c10cc67fe8b65aecdc0be7bdda61c79e4e219

This causes either compilation failures on certain targets (Windows) or crashes at runtime (Windows, OS X). It's also slow.

Testing before/after the integrate with `tests/e2e/models/resnet50_fake_weights.mlir` for x64 CPU on Windows I get this diff showing the additional allocations:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75337/212376572-46063f5e-5c6d-4e77-8215-1298a45206d0.png)

This seems to be the root cause (the first diff in the compilation):
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75337/212379861-fd6cbad0-772c-4efd-b184-57d0920fdb8c.png)

Executable before TileAndDistributeToWorkgroups pass:
```mlir

#map = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2, d3) -> (d0, d1, d2, d3)>
#map1 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2, d3) -> (d3)>
#map2 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2, d3, d4) -> (d0 * 2 + d3, d1 * 2 + d4, d2)>
#map3 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2, d3, d4) -> (d3, d4)>
#map4 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2, d3, d4) -> (d0, d1, d2)>

#map6 = affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d1)>
#map7 = affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d1, d0)>
#map8 = affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0)>
#map9 = affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>
#map10 = affine_map<(d0) -> ()>
#map11 = affine_map<(d0, d1) -> ()>
#pipeline_layout = #hal.pipeline.layout<push_constants = 0, sets = [<0, bindings = [<0, storage_buffer, ReadOnly>, <1, storage_buffer>]>]>
#device_target_llvm_cpu = #hal.device.target<"llvm-cpu", {executable_targets = [#executable_target_embedded_elf_x86_64_]}>
module attributes {hal.device.targets = [#device_target_llvm_cpu]} {
  hal.executable private @predict_dispatch_3 {
    hal.executable.variant public @embedded_elf_x86_64, target = #executable_target_embedded_elf_x86_64_ {
      hal.executable.export public @predict_dispatch_3_generic_56x56x64x3x3 ordinal(0) layout(#pipeline_layout) {
      ^bb0(%arg0: !hal.device, %arg1: index, %arg2: index, %arg3: index, %arg4: index, %arg5: index):
        %x, %y, %z = flow.dispatch.workgroup_count_from_dag_root %arg1, %arg2, %arg3, %arg4, %arg5
        hal.return %x, %y, %z : index, index, index
      }
      builtin.module {
        func.func @predict_dispatch_3_generic_56x56x64x3x3() {
          %c3846080 = arith.constant 3846080 : index
          %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
          %cst = arith.constant dense<0xFF800000> : tensor<56x56x64xf32>
          %0 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(0) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c3846080) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:tensor<114x114x64xf32>>
          %1 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(1) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c0) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<writeonly:tensor<56x56x64xf32>>
          %2 = flow.dispatch.tensor.load %0, offsets = [0, 0, 0], sizes = [114, 114, 64], strides = [1, 1, 1] : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:tensor<114x114x64xf32>> -> tensor<114x114x64xf32>
          %3 = tensor.empty() : tensor<3x3xf32>
          %4 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [#map2, #map3, #map4], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel", "parallel", "reduction", "reduction"]} ins(%2, %3 : tensor<114x114x64xf32>, tensor<3x3xf32>) outs(%cst : tensor<56x56x64xf32>) {

            %5 = arith.maxf %out, %in : f32
            linalg.yield %5 : f32
          } -> tensor<56x56x64xf32>
          flow.dispatch.tensor.store %4, %1, offsets = [0, 0, 0], sizes = [56, 56, 64], strides = [1, 1, 1] : tensor<56x56x64xf32> -> !flow.dispatch.tensor<writeonly:tensor<56x56x64xf32>>

issue.body:
This change replaces the `outs` operands of Linalg ops that are splat constants with `fill` of that value. Having constants operands for `outs` causes bufferization issues downstream (which are harder to fix, though in theory whether the outs is a constant or not it shouldnt matter. The general case fix looks very similar to what happens here anyway).

Fixes #11830
